quotes.text: You can use this public preview feature by including the version header `2025-11-17.preview` or a later preview version header in your API request.
Stripe and Klarna accept well-formed supplementary purchase data but don’t provide feedback on whether the specific data you send qualifies for improved outcomes.
You send Klarna-specific supplementary purchase data through the `payment_method_options.klarna.supplementary_purchase_data` parameter when you

findings: The November and May prose agree on public-preview 2025-11-17.preview or later preview header, Klarna-only eight verticals, PaymentIntent create/update/confirm parameter, no fee change or validation feedback, and full-replacement/preserve/unset semantics (new raw lines 9-59,349-416; old raw lines 8-58,564-705). Existing source lines 19-29 accurately summarize the parameter and update rules, but source line 17 incorrectly narrows the allowed API header to exactly 2025-11-17.preview rather than that header or a later preview version; this is a material baseline version-gate correction, not a November change.

All examples changed from Node SDK with payment_method_types: ['klarna'] to curl with automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true, including create and update examples for insurance, vouchers, events, train, bus, ferry, organized trips, and marketplace sellers (old raw lines 60-561; new raw lines 61-347; diff lines 25-708). The parameter keys and example data remain equivalent, but the example selection mechanism differs; automatic selection does not prove Klarna is offered or authorized for any actual payment.

New and old both use server-side secret-key examples on PaymentIntent creation/update; the new curl syntax is a presentation/API example switch, not a documented change to client behavior, PaymentIntent success, or underwriting outcome (old raw lines 60-115,564-705; new raw lines 61-84,349-416).

New raw lines 90-347 still refer full per-vertical field definitions to versioned preview API reference links; the linked schemas were not part of these pinned captures. Insurance is a standalone primary product in this vertical, whereas nested insurance examples for events and transport are example fields (new raw lines 90-94,138-162,165-319).

The current source lists only the May raw in frontmatter and Raw Sources and has no canonical_url field (source lines 1-9,31-33). The November capture is the same canonical page with newer dated curl/automatic-payment-methods examples (old raw lines 1-2,62-115; new raw lines 1-2,63-84); retain May provenance, add the November raw route and exact canonical URL without inferring changed eligibility.

Current source lines 13 and 23 and the related BNPL concept line 231 say supplementary data improves acceptance rates without the captured potential/variable-impact qualification. Both captures say it can increase approvals, impact varies and well-formed data gets no feedback whether it qualifies for improved outcomes (old raw lines 21,31,35; new raw lines 22,32,36). The concept's preview header is also terse (wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md:231,268).

source_assessments.reason: The raw behavior is unchanged, but the mapped source needs a narrow baseline version-gate and outcome-qualification correction plus the missing exact canonical URL and dated November raw route.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/supplementary-purchase-data, the November capture documents a Klarna-only public preview for eight verticals, usable with API header 2025-11-17.preview or a later preview version (new raw lines 9-53). A server-side PaymentIntent create, update or confirm carries payment_method_options.klarna.supplementary_purchase_data; arrays can contain multiple entries and verticals, with replacement per updated vertical, omitted verticals preserved, and empty strings clearing one or all (new raw lines 55-59,349-416). Well-formed data gets no feedback on improved-outcome qualification, fees are unchanged, and authorization improvement is only possible and variable (new raw lines 22,31-36). The May guide establishes the same behavior (old raw lines 8-58,564-705). source-stripe-klarna-supplementary-data.md correctly summarizes the parameter and update rules (source lines 19-29) but incorrectly restricts the preview header to one exact version, implies an unqualified benefit, and lacks the November raw and canonical URL provenance (source lines 1-17,23,31-33). Neither capture proves approval or payment success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/supplementary-purchase-data, the preview rule, eight verticals, PaymentIntent identity and update semantics are unchanged (old raw lines 8-58,564-705; new raw lines 9-59,349-416). The visible delta is example presentation: May Node SDK examples explicitly use payment_method_types ['klarna'], while November curl examples enable automatic_payment_methods; both are server-side secret-key examples, and this proves no Klarna eligibility, authorization, client behavior or payment success (old raw lines 60-115; new raw lines 61-84). source-stripe-klarna-supplementary-data.md needs the later-preview-header allowance, exact canonical URL and both dated raw routes, and potential rather than guaranteed acceptance wording (source lines 1-17,23,31-33; old raw lines 10,21,31,35; new raw lines 11,22,32,36). The related BNPL concept line 231 needs the same outcome qualification and preview-version precision. Linked field schemas remain outside the pinned captures.
